name: Joshua
bio:
Joshua is the son of Nun of the tribe of Ephraim, originally named Hoshea, Moses' most important aide and eventual successor, first appearing in Exodus 17 — when the Amalekites attacked Israel, Moses instructed Joshua to choose men and go fight them, while Moses himself stood on the hilltop with Aaron and Hur, holding up his hands in prayer; Joshua defeated the Amalekites as a result (Exodus 17:8-13).

Joshua appears repeatedly afterward as Moses' closest attendant — accompanying him up Mount Sinai (Exodus 24:13) and keeping watch at the tabernacle (Exodus 33:11). When Moses sent the leaders of the twelve tribes to spy out Canaan, he renamed Hoshea "Joshua," meaning "the LORD is salvation" (Numbers 13:16). Ten of the spies brought back an exaggerated bad report, but Joshua, along with Caleb, insisted the land was exceedingly good and urged the people not to fear or rebel against the LORD; the congregation nearly stoned them both for it. God responded by promising that of that entire generation, only Joshua and Caleb would enter the promised land (Numbers 14:6-10, 30).

Before his death, Moses, at the LORD's command, formally commissioned Joshua before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, laying his hands on him to transfer leadership of the people to him (Numbers 27:18-23). Joshua's full story of leading Israel into Canaan and conquering the promised land is recorded in the book of Joshua.
